name: PugiSwift
baseline: XMLCoder (Codable over Foundation XMLParser) and Fuzi (libxml2)
verdict_reason: It parsed a 212 KB file 14x as often as XMLCoder and 3.7x as often as Fuzi in one test. Plain Foundation XMLParser with a delegate was not measured, so the gap to the actual default is unknown, and the method (one one-second loop per parser) is thin.
tier_reason: Benchmark code is public (PugiSwiftComparisons) and run in release mode, but hardware, OS and Swift version are not stated and each parser runs one one-second loop.
claimed_speedup: 757 parses/s vs 207 (Fuzi) and 54 (XMLCoder) on a 212kb file: 3.7x Fuzi and 14x XMLCoder (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Parsing a 212 KB XML file of <record> elements (11 string and integer fields each) into Swift structs, counting completed parses in one second
toolchain: Release mode, debugger off; Swift version not stated
platforms: Apple platforms and Linux (server use with Vapor per README)
one_liner: Swift macros over the pugixml C++ parser; 14x XMLCoder and 3.7x Fuzi on a 212 KB file in its author's test.
how_it_is_fast: pugixml parses the document in place into a compact DOM with few allocations, and Swift macros (@Node, @Attribute, @Element) generate the code that maps nodes to struct fields. XMLCoder instead drives Foundation's XMLParser callbacks into an intermediate tree and runs Codable over it.
use_it_when: Decoding large or frequent XML documents into fixed Swift structs
Server-side XML ingestion where XMLCoder shows up in profiles
skip_it_when: You need XPath or CSS queries over arbitrary documents (Fuzi, Kanna)
Streaming very large files: pugixml builds a full DOM in memory
caveats: One one-second loop per parser, no warm-up or repeated trials.
Hardware, OS and Swift version not stated.
Foundation XMLParser used directly (SAX delegate, no Codable) was not measured.
tradeoffs: Macro-generated mapping is less flexible than query-based access

evidence.quote: The test was in Release mode with the debugger turned off. Comparisons were made against [Fuzi](https://github.com/cezheng/Fuzi.git) and [XMLCoder](https://github.com/CoreOffice/XMLCoder.git).
